title: Hands — from intent to work
task: Create a crafted 60–90 second Remotion launch film for Hands, the computer-use assistant, aimed at early-stage accelerator reviewers. Use Astra low and return to Jev for checked render and delivery. Tell a simple story: a person knows the outcome but must coordinate tools; Hands can take a request, involve a specialist, execute bounded next steps and accept corrections; show two actual inspected outputs supplied in the runtime evidence; close with one concrete next milestone. Do not turn the pitch into a technical audit or a disclaimer slideshow. Brand it Hands. Make the motion, music and companion website feel carefully designed.

creativeBrief.direction: Ink, warm ivory and electric cobalt. Large concise type, varied asymmetric compositions, kinetic opening, animated workflow nodes, moving task chips, deliberate reveals of two real output images, and a confident closing hold. Use at least four distinct layouts and three tones. Show visual evidence at a readable scale. No generic card grid or uniform bullet slides.
creativeBrief.story: Original opening tension and concise product promise; one development prototype label; two useful real output demonstrations; Jev → specialist → Jev execution diagram with a correction path; one plain-language next milestone. Intended users can be described as builders, students and researchers without pretending there are existing customers. Keep evidence detail in a sidecar.
creativeBrief.soundtrack: Required original minimal-electronic instrumental score: music={style:minimal-electronic,tempoBpm:112,intensity:0.7,seed:73,gainDb:-4}. No narration. Purposeful build, restrained beat and clean opening/closing fades. Never describe it as silent.
creativeBrief.renderer: Trusted1280x72024fps Remotion. storyboard.design={theme:editorial-cobalt,motion:expressive}. Scene layout supports kinetic-title,workflow,task-field,artifact-stage,editorial,statement,closing-mark. Use explicit workflow nodes (3 or4) and terse captions. artifact-stage needs supplied actual artifactImage ID. No generated executable renderer/config or fictional capabilities.
creativeBrief.website: A strong launch-film viewing experience, with beautifully composed title/player/chapters, working play/pause, sound toggle, captions, seek and fullscreen controls. Deliberate mobile layout and nearby readable scene copy. Keep evidence collapsed or linked; do not fill the player site with audit metadata. No audible autoplay. Use native button click handlers rather than form submission because the preview sandbox forbids forms.
creativeBrief.tone: Direct, useful, specific and confident. Never invent customers, revenue, YC endorsement, biography or measured end-to-end reliability. A brief development-prototype label and one future milestone provide honest scope. Omit performance numbers for this film.

sources.use: Current implemented product description; does not establish general reliability or actual task completion.

The final film has at least four varied layouts, three tones and actual intra-scene motion; contact sheets alone do not prove motion.
Two distinct actual inspected Hands artifact images, bound by runtime IDs and hashes, support the demo. No invented screenshot or claimed recording of a live desktop.
The generated evidence ledger maps concrete claims to supplied repository/runtime evidence, with short honest development scope and no invented traction or speed claim.
Original music is encoded as AAC and verified audible, non-clipping, with arrangement variation and fades. The sound controls actually affect playback.
The player works on desktop and mobile: play/pause, seek, sound, captions, fullscreen and chapter controls. Local page navigation works in the real opaque-origin artifact sandbox.
Inspect real motion samples and readable scene stills, plus the actual player views and interactions. Report specific observed limitations; do not conflate model scores with user taste.
